issue: far-tax-02 is not self-contained: its stem says 'Using the previous item' and omits the pretax income ($600,000), tax-exempt interest ($30,000) and fines ($12,000) needed to answer. Practice sets and review queues are shuffled, so the 'previous item' is usually not far-tax-01. It also shows far-tax-01's key ($111,720) as option (a) and in its explanation, so whichever order they appear in, one item gives away the other's answer.
evidence: src/lib/quiz.ts:84-86 shuffles the eligible items (shuffle(...).sort(by attempts), then shuffle(picked)), and mixed and mastery sets interleave modules (lines 95-98, 114-135). Seen on its own, far-tax-02 gives only the $50,000 depreciation difference, the 21% rate and no beginning balances, so total expense can't be computed. Recomputed with far-tax-01's facts: current (600,000 − 30,000 + 12,000 − 50,000) × 21% = 111,720, deferred 50,000 × 21% = 10,500, total 122,220. That's the key, but it can only be reached with facts from another item. Option (a) '$111,720 — That's only current tax' is far-tax-01's key.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ checks 3 and 6 (stem completeness; one item revealing the answer to another)
fix: Rewrite far-tax-02 to stand alone: 'Pretax book income is $600,000, including $30,000 of tax-exempt interest and $12,000 of nondeductible fines. Tax depreciation exceeds book depreciation by $50,000 (arising this year). The enacted rate is 21%, and there are no beginning deferred balances. What is total income tax expense?' To stop the two items cueing each other, change far-tax-02's numbers (e.g., pretax $700,000, so total = 21% × 682,000 = 143,220) or merge the pair into one two-part item.

issue: The journal scorer marks the lesson's own entry format wrong. The lesson's JE block records the provision with two expense lines ('Income tax expense — current' and 'Income tax expense — deferred'). The TBS keys accept only one combined 'Income tax expense' debit, and scoreJournal matches line by line, so a correct entry that splits expense into its current and deferred amounts loses 2 cells.
evidence: Lesson lines 99-107: Dr IT expense—current 159,600; Dr IT expense—deferred 6,300. r3 key: Dr Income tax expense 123,750 / Dr DTA 5,000 / Cr Income taxes payable 113,750 / Cr DTL 15,000. Simulated src/lib/tbsScoring.ts scoreJournal on the response Dr IT expense 113,750, Dr IT expense 10,000, Dr DTA 5,000, Cr ITP 113,750, Cr DTL 15,000 (balanced, 128,750 = 128,750). The expected 123,750 line finds no match (wrong); one IT-expense line is 'blamed' and the other becomes an 'Extra line' (wrong). Result: 3 of 5 cells (60%) for a correct entry. u10 works the same way: 286,650 + 23,100 split across two lines scores 3 of 5 (maxLines 5 allows it).
source: ASC 740-10-50-9 (current and deferred components of tax expense are separately disclosed, so separate lines are standard practice); src/lib/tbsScoring.ts scoreJournal
fix: Do one of the following. (a) Change the lesson's JE block to a single 'Income tax expense 165,900' debit and add a note: 'current 159,600 + deferred 6,300'. (b) Add the accounts 'Income tax expense — current' and 'Income tax expense — deferred' to both TBS account lists and key the split entry. (c) Change scoreJournal to sum same-account, same-side lines before matching. Option (c) fixes the problem for every JE TBS.

issue: These items are pure recall but are labeled skill 'analysis' and difficulty 3, two skill levels too high. far-tax-27 ('How are DTLs classified? All as noncurrent') is a near-copy of far-tax-07, which is correctly labeled remembering/1. far-tax-20 ('Is a DTL recognized on nondeductible goodwill? No') recalls a single scope exception.
evidence: far-tax-07: remembering/1. far-tax-27: analysis/3. The stems have 0.86 Jaccard similarity (cues.md), and the options (by related asset / all current / all noncurrent / by reversal date) are effectively the same. Neither item asks the candidate to examine interrelationships or evidence (the Blueprint's definition of Analysis); each is a one-fact yes/no or classification recall. Both labels feed the FAR skill-mix targets (R&U 5-15%, App 45-55%, Analysis 35-45%; content/sections/far.yaml).
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Set skill 'remembering' and difficulty 1 on both items. Better still, replace far-tax-27 with a new item, since it duplicates far-tax-07 (see the redundancy finding).

issue: Labels are inflated by one level. Several one-step computations are labeled analysis/difficulty 3; far-tax-21 to -28 appear to have been batch-labeled. These are the simplest items in the module, so the easy-to-hard progression is inverted and the analysis share is overstated. far-tax-14 is recall labeled application. far-tax-06 asks only 'where' the effect is recognized, yet it carries calc: true.
evidence: Recomputed, every one is a single operation. 21: 30,000 × 25% = 7,500. 22: 30,000 × 21% = 6,300. 23: 40,000 × 25% = 10,000. 24: (200,000 − 10,000) × 25% = 47,500. 25: 47,500 + 5,000 = 52,500. 28: 80% × 90,000 = 72,000. x3-08: 950,000 × 21% = 199,500. chk2: read 200,000 from the stem. By contrast, far-tax-11 (50,000 × 21%) is labeled application/1 and far-tax-01 (four adjustments) application/2. Practice and exam pool labels as they stand: application 15, remembering 4, analysis 14 (42%). Corrected (with finding 003): remembering 7 (21%), application 21 (64%), analysis 5 (15%). That is well outside FAR's 35-45% analysis target. far-tax-06's answer needs no number; the 32,000 appears only in the explanation.
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel 21, 22, 23, 24, 25 and 28 as application, difficulty 1 (22 may be 2). Relabel x3-08 as application/1 and chk2 as application. Relabel far-tax-14 as remembering/1. Remove calc from far-tax-06 (or set it false). Then add genuine analysis items (see the coverage finding) so the module's analysis share is real.

issue: Some distractor rationales and trap labels do not describe the error that produces the number. Four distractors say only 'Not the computation.' (trap 'distractor-number'), although each comes from a specific misconception, and one cannot be produced by any plausible error. Other trap labels name the wrong misconception.
evidence: Each distractor reproduced from its stem in python. 21(c) 22,500 = 30,000 × (1 − 25%): an after-tax or net amount; rationale 'Not the computation.' 22(c) 9,000 = 30,000 × 30%: no 30% rate appears anywhere in the stem, so no plausible error yields it (the plausible errors give 7,500 at the current rate, 1,200 for the rate change only, or 13,800 with both rates applied). 24(b) 52,500 = (200,000 + 10,000) × 25%: adds the muni interest, a wrong-sign error; rationale 'Not the computation.' 24(c) 2,500 = 10,000 × 25%: the tax effect of the muni alone (partial-computation), but trap is 'reversed'. 28(c) 80,000 = 80% × 100,000: applies the 80% to the NOL rather than to taxable income; rationale 'Not the computation.' 19(d) 74,000 = 0.3×100,000 + 0.3×80,000 + 0.4×50,000, the expected value: a wrong-rule (wrong measurement method) error, but trap is 'wrong-classification'. 08(a) 1,000,000: recognizing the full position (all-or-nothing) is a wrong-rule error, not 'partial-computation'. x3-06(a) 63,000 = 300,000 × 21%: rationale says 'Applies the current 21% rate', but the stem states no current rate; 21% is the Year 2 enacted rate.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 2 (trap label matches the misconception)
fix: Rewrite the rationales and traps. 21(c): 'This is the difference net of tax (30,000 × 75%); the DTL is the tax effect, 30,000 × 25%', trap partial-computation. 22(c): replace 9,000 with 1,200 ('only the 4-point rate change') or 13,800, with a matching rationale. 24(b): 'Adds the muni interest instead of subtracting it: 210,000 × 25%', trap wrong-sign. 24(c): trap partial-computation. 28(c): 'Applies 80% to the NOL instead of to taxable income', trap wrong-rule. 19(d): trap wrong-rule. 08(a): trap wrong-rule. x3-06(a): 'Applies the Year 2 rate (21%) to the whole difference'.

issue: Several calc items have explanations that restate the rule but never show the computation, in either the item-level explanation or the correct-choice explanation.
evidence: 11: 'Future deductions create a deferred tax asset.' (no 50,000 × 21% = 10,500). 16: 'The 40% not expected to be realized.' (no 200,000 × 40% = 80,000). 19: no cumulative table (100,000 at 30%; 80,000 at 30% + 30% = 60%, which is over 50%). 22: 'Use the enacted rate for the reversal year.' (no 30,000 × 21% = 6,300). 26: no cumulative table (30% + 25% = 55% at 80,000). 28: 'limited to 80% of taxable income' (no 80% × 90,000 = 72,000; 28,000 carries forward).
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 4 (explanations state the rule and show the computation)
fix: Add the one-line computation to each item-level explanation, for example 19: 'Cumulative: $100,000 30%; $80,000 60% (> 50%) → recognize $80,000.' 28: '80% × $90,000 = $72,000 deductible; $28,000 carries forward indefinitely.'

issue: Answer cues. In chk1 and 03 the key is by far the longest option, and the only one hedged as a complete rule. far-tax-20's key is the 2-character 'No', and distractor (c) 'Yes, as a DTA' contradicts its own stem, which asks about a DTL. In far-x3-26 the only absolutes ('Only when', 'Never ... always') sit in the distractors. far-tax-25's stem gives far-tax-24's key ($47,500 current tax).
evidence: Option lengths in characters: chk1 key 59 vs 34-41 for the distractors; 03 key 63 vs 28-45, with 'always' only in distractor (a); 20 key 2 vs 13-24. x3-26: (b) 'Only when ... remote', (d) 'Never; ... always'. far-tax-24's key (d) is $47,500; far-tax-25 opens 'Current tax expense is $47,500 ...'. Sessions are shuffled, so 25 often comes before 24.
fix: chk1: shorten the key to 'Warranty costs accrued before they are deductible', or lengthen the distractors to match. 03: give each option a parallel full clause (e.g., 'The rate in effect when the difference originated'; 'The enacted rate for the reversal year'), and drop 'always'. 20: rewrite the options as parallel statements ('No DTL; the excess of book goodwill over tax basis is an exception' / 'A DTL at the enacted rate' / 'A DTL only when goodwill is impaired' / 'A DTL measured at the effective rate'), or retire the item (see the scope finding). x3-26: give one distractor a qualifier and soften the others ('When realization is probable but not certain'). 25: change its current tax to a figure unrelated to far-tax-24 (e.g., $61,000).

issue: The key 'Either way, by policy' is vague, and the distractor pair frames it. 'Either way' refers to the other options, and the only alternative they offer is 'operating expense'. ASC 740-10-45-25 permits interest as income taxes or interest expense, and penalties as income taxes or another expense classification. Interest expense is usually nonoperating. The two 'Only ...' distractors also signal that the hedged option is the key.
evidence: Options: (a) 'Only as income tax expense', (b) 'Either way, by policy', (c) 'Only as operating expense', (d) 'As a reduction of revenue'. Choices are shuffled per session (src/lib/random.ts:43), so 'either way' has no fixed referent. ASC 740-10-45-25 ties the alternatives to interest expense (for interest) and to another expense classification (for penalties), not to 'operating expense' generally.
fix: Key: 'As income tax expense, or as interest expense (interest) and another expense line (penalties), by an accounting policy election applied consistently and disclosed.' Distractors: 'Only as income tax expense'; 'Only as interest expense, never as income tax'; 'As an adjustment to the liability for unrecognized tax benefits with no expense'. Keep the policy-election explanation.

issue: Redundancy. The same one-step facts are drilled the same way more than three times, while major ASC 740 topics get no items at all.
evidence: Clusters. (1) Noncurrent classification: far-tax-07 and far-tax-27 (0.86 stem similarity, same four options), plus flashcard fc7 and a lesson takeaway. (2) VA = DTA × % not realized: chk2, far-tax-16, far-tax-23, far-x3-07 (16 and 23 have 0.65 similarity). (3) DTA/DTL = one difference × rate: far-tax-05, -11, -21, -22, x3-18. (4) Basic current/total provision with a permanent item: far-tax-01/02, -13, -24/25, x3-08, plus all three TBS. With 28 practice MCQs, about 18 sit in these four clusters.
fix: Keep one or two items per cluster. Replace far-tax-27, far-tax-23, far-tax-21 and far-tax-25 with items on untested topics: the ASU 2023-09 rate reconciliation, intraperiod allocation with the with-and-without approach, a VA judgment from mixed evidence (cumulative losses vs. DTL reversals and tax-planning strategies), a rate change applied to a DTA with an existing VA, and a UTP that fails the recognition step.

issue: far-tax-20 tests deferred taxes on nondeductible goodwill recognized in an acquisition (ASC 805-740). Business combinations and goodwill are BAR scope under the 2024-2026 Blueprints, and the repo's own notes say this content is not built as FAR content. The item isn't marked optional, so it goes into mixed sets, diagnostics and mocks. The lesson never teaches it.
evidence: docs/BLUEPRINT_NOTES.md lines 63-65 list 'business combinations (acquisition method)' as moved to BAR and 'not built as FAR content'. review/reference/far-standards.md §1c lists business combinations as BAR (verified) and goodwill as BAR per Becker (conflict with the repo notes). review/reference/blueprint-notes.md says FAR Area II.F covers finite-lived intangibles only. lesson.md has no mention of goodwill or acquisitions. The schema's optional flag (src/content/schema.ts) exists for exactly this case.
fix: Set optional: true on far-tax-20, or replace it with an in-scope item such as a DTL on equity-method undistributed earnings, or a DTA on a deductible temporary difference with a partial VA.

issue: Lesson-item alignment gaps. The practice items test two things the lesson never teaches. (1) The cumulative-probability method for measuring an uncertain tax position: the lesson says only 'the largest amount that is more than 50% likely', with no table or worked example, yet far-tax-08, -19 and -26 all need a cumulative tabulation in which no single outcome exceeds 50%. (2) The policy election for classifying interest and penalties on unrecognized tax benefits (far-tax-14): not mentioned anywhere in the lesson. (The goodwill item far-tax-20 is covered by a separate finding.)
evidence: lesson.md lines 117-119 give two-step UTP text only. In 08 the outcomes are 35/30/25/10%, in 19 30/30/40% and in 26 30/25/25/20%. None reaches 50% alone, so a learner who applies 'more than 50% likely' to single outcomes gets $0 or is stuck. lesson.md never pairs 'cumulative' with probability. The word appears only as 'cumulative temporary differences' (line 71), 'cumulative excess' (line 124) and 'cumulative recent losses' (line 113). 'Penalties' appears only in the permanent-difference table (line 56), never in connection with UTBs.
fix: Add a short faded block after 'Uncertain tax positions': a 4-outcome table with a cumulative-probability column, where the learner computes the recognized benefit and the liability for unrecognized tax benefits (e.g., $1,000,000 claimed: 35% / 65% cumulative → recognize $800,000; UTB liability = $200,000 × 21% = $42,000). Add one bullet: 'Interest and penalties on UTBs: classify as income tax expense or as interest/other expense, by policy election; apply consistently and disclose.'

issue: ASU 2023-09 income tax disclosures are testable in 2026, but the lesson mentions them only in a parenthetical, 'expanded for public entities', and no item or TBS tests them. That wording also misses the requirement that applies to all entities: income taxes paid, disaggregated by federal, state and foreign, and by jurisdictions at or above 5%.
evidence: lesson.md line 141: 'a rate reconciliation (expanded for public entities by ASU 2023-09)'. review/reference/far-standards.md §2a lists ASU 2023-09 as eligible from 1/1/2025 (verified). PBEs give a tabular reconciliation in both percent and amount across 8 categories, with items of at least 5% of pretax income × statutory rate shown separately. All entities disaggregate income taxes paid. Non-PBEs describe their reconciling items qualitatively. None of the 33 practice and exam MCQs or the 3 TBS involves a rate reconciliation or taxes-paid disclosure.
fix: Expand the 'Presentation and disclosure' bullet. PBEs: tabular reconciliation, percent and amount, 8 categories, 5% threshold. All entities: income taxes paid by federal, state and foreign and by jurisdictions of 5% or more. Non-PBEs: qualitative description of reconciling items. Use the lesson's worked example as a mini reconciliation (statutory 168,000 at 21% × 800,000; muni −4,200; fines +2,100; total 165,900 = 20.7%). Add one practice MCQ, or a TBS part, on it.

issue: Several ASC 740 topics the lesson teaches get no practice. No MCQ or TBS covers: intraperiod allocation beyond a recall item; a valuation-allowance judgment from mixed evidence; a change in VA flowing into deferred tax expense; remeasuring a DTA, or a DTL with beginning balances, for a rate change in a computation; a UTP that fails recognition, or the UTB liability amount; the balance-sheet approach with carrying amount vs. tax basis for a liability (e.g., warranty); and the ASU 2023-09 rate reconciliation. The module has no genuine analysis-level item; once the labels are corrected, analysis is about 15% against FAR's 35-45%.
evidence: Mapped the 33 practice/exam MCQs and 3 TBS by topic. Basic provision or deferred measurement: 01, 02, 04, 05, 11, 13, 17, 18, 21, 22, 24, 25, x3-06, x3-08, x3-18 and all 3 TBS. VA percent: chk2, 16, 23, x3-07, x3-26. UTP measurement: 08, 19, 26. Classification: 07, 27. Rate change: 06, 12. NOL: 10, 28. Intraperiod: 15 (recall only). The three TBS are all a one-year provision with no beginning VA, no rate change and no UTP; r3 and x3 add nothing beyond the lesson worked example. Corrected skill mix (findings 003/004): R 7 / App 21 / Ana 5.
source: AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint Area III.D (accounting for income taxes); content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Add 4-6 analysis-level items, or rework one TBS. Candidates: (a) a rate change enacted mid-year that remeasures beginning DTL and DTA balances, with a VA; (b) a with-and-without intraperiod allocation between continuing operations and discontinued operations or OCI; (c) judging the VA from given positive and negative evidence; (d) a UTP that fails recognition, with the UTB liability and interest; (e) completing an ASU 2023-09 rate reconciliation. Converting far-tbs-x3-income-taxes into a multi-year rate-change/VA simulation would cover several of these at once.

issue: The exam-pool (mock) TBS is a near-copy of the lesson's worked example and has only 6 numeric cells, yet it is budgeted 20 minutes. Its book-tax differences match the lesson exactly ($60,000 excess tax depreciation, $30,000 warranty, $20,000 muni, $10,000 fines, 21%); only pretax income changes, from $800,000 to $900,000. A mock item that repeats a worked example measures memory of the example, not transfer. The 20-minute estimate overstates the time needed and distorts mock pacing.
evidence: Lesson worked block (lines 77-97): 800,000 − 20,000 + 10,000 − 60,000 + 30,000; DTL 12,600, DTA 6,300. x3: 900,000 − 60,000 + 30,000 − 20,000 + 10,000 = 860,000; DTL 12,600, DTA 6,300 (identical); total 186,900; ETR 20.77%. r3 (practice) has the same structure plus a JE and is also 20 minutes. x3 has 6 single-step cells and no dropdown, JE, beginning balances or judgment; a realistic time is about 8-10 minutes.
source: Review brief §2 per-TBS checks (skill and time estimate realistic); §3 mock exams
fix: Change x3's differences and add depth: beginning DTL and DTA balances, a rate change enacted in 2025 for 2027 and later, a partial VA, and a JE or a dropdown classification part. Keep 20 minutes only if it reaches that scope (about 12-15 cells); otherwise set minutes to about 10.

issue: The x3 exhibit does not say whether the municipal bond interest and the fines are included in pretax financial income. r3 and u10 state it explicitly ('included in book income' / 'expensed for books'); x3 lists 'Interest on municipal bonds: $20,000' and 'Fines paid ... $10,000' without saying where they sit.
evidence: The key assumes both are inside the $900,000 (860,000 = 900,000 − 20,000 + 10,000 − 60,000 + 30,000). The r3 exhibit reads 'Municipal bond interest included in book income' and 'Nondeductible fines included in book expenses'.
fix: Reword as 'Interest on municipal bonds included in pretax financial income: $20,000' and 'Fines for environmental violations (nondeductible), expensed for books: $10,000'.

issue: The shortcut 'total tax expense = rate × (pretax income adjusted for permanent differences)' is stated without its conditions. The lesson's worked-example insight says temporary differences 'don't change total tax expense's relationship to book income', and far-tax-13's explanation reads '21% × (pretax income + permanent differences)'. The shortcut holds only with one enacted rate for all years, no rate change and no VA change. The lesson's own faded example breaks it. The '+' also mis-states the sign for income such as muni interest.
evidence: Faded example: the Year 1 originating difference is 400,000 − 200,000 = 200,000. At 21% that gives 42,000, but the remeasurement to 25% makes deferred expense 100,000 − 42,000 = 58,000, so the 'same relationship to book income' claim fails. far-tax-13 formula: with $20,000 of muni interest instead of fines, the correct total is 21% × (800,000 − 20,000) = 163,800, but '+ permanent differences' gives 21% × 820,000 = 172,200.
fix: Lesson insight: add 'when a single enacted rate applies to all years and no valuation allowance changes'. far-tax-13 explanation: 'Total = 161,700 current + 10,500 deferred = 172,200; check: 21% × (800,000 + 20,000 nondeductible fines) when one flat rate applies.'

issue: The far-tax-09 explanation says key-person life insurance proceeds 'are never taxable'. That is overstated: under IRC §101(j), proceeds of employer-owned life insurance are taxable above premiums paid unless the notice-and-consent requirements and an exception are met. The FAR treatment (permanent difference) is right; only the absolute is wrong.
evidence: Explanation: 'Premiums on officers' life insurance with the company as beneficiary are never deductible, and proceeds are never taxable — permanent.' §264(a)(1) does deny the premium deduction, and §101(a) excludes proceeds, subject to §101(j).
fix: Reword as: '... premiums are nondeductible (§264) and the death proceeds are generally excluded from income (§101), so neither reverses: a permanent difference.'

issue: The lesson has a single pre-question, and it primes only permanent vs. temporary differences. Nothing primes the lesson's other big ideas: enacted-rate remeasurement, the valuation allowance and the UTP two-step. The third objective (valuation allowances and UTPs, analysis) has no Blueprint `task` link, though the other two objectives do.
evidence: Frontmatter: preQuestions: [far-tax-pre1] (muni interest, a permanent difference). Objective 3 has no task field.
fix: Add one or two pre-questions, e.g., 'A new rate is enacted in December for future years. When do existing DTLs change?' and 'A DTA's realization is 40% likely. Is the full DTA reported?'. Add task: 'Calculate income tax expense, deferred tax assets, and deferred tax liabilities' (or the VA/UTP representative task) to objective 3.

issue: Flashcard fc3 gives total tax expense as 'Current + (Δ DTL − Δ DTA)' with no valuation-allowance term. The FAR formula sheet states the same rule with '(+ Δvaluation allowance)', so the two places differ, and a learner using fc3 would miss VA changes.
evidence: content/far/review/far-formulas.md line 49: 'Current (taxable income × rate) + ΔDTL − ΔDTA (+ Δvaluation allowance)'. fc3: 'Current (taxable income × rate) + deferred (Δ DTL − Δ DTA).' The lesson takeaway (line 32) also omits the VA term.
fix: fc3 back: 'Current (taxable income × rate) + deferred (Δ DTL − Δ DTA net of valuation allowance, i.e., + increase in VA).' Make the same change to the lesson takeaway.
